question: How do you get people to save more without asking them to give anything up today?
answer: Ask them to save out of future pay rises. In Thaler and Benartzi's 'Save More Tomorrow' plan, workers agreed now to save part of each future raise, so take-home pay never fell. At the first company to try it, average saving rates rose from 3.5% to 13.6% in under four years.
move: Commit your future self to the sacrifice your present self won't make.
simply: Promising to give away half of next birthday's money is much easier than giving away half of today's.
why: It works for any change that hurts now and pays later, from savings to exercise: schedule the cost for a moment you won't feel it.
source: Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein, Nudge, 2008
reference: Richard H. Thaler and Cass R. Sunstein, Nudge (Yale University Press, 2008), ch. 6
